channel.description: UN News - Global perspective Human stories | Women

item.title: ‘Women are not victims’: Türk calls for women to be at the heart of peace and security
item.description: Women must be at the centre of efforts to prevent conflict and build lasting peace, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Gender equality woefully off track, new UN report reveals
item.description: At the current rate of progress, gender equality would take 171 years to achieve, a new UN report finds as institutions built to advance gains are being defunded and demobilised.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: In Gaza, women-headed households face ‘impossible choices’ to survive
item.description: In war-torn Gaza, a growing number of women-headed households face “impossible decisions” every day, amid ongoing Israeli airstrikes and still-scarce resources, UN humanitarians said on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Gloria Steinem: A voice for women, to the very end
item.description: Gloria Steinem, the journalist and women's rights campaigner who became one of the most influential voices of the feminist movement, has died at the age of 92. In an announcement on Instagram, her family said she had passed away on Wednesday at her home in New York City, surrounded by some of the many who loved her.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Tate brothers’ US extradition case a ‘step towards accountability,’ says independent expert
item.description: An independent UN human rights expert has welcomed ongoing proceedings in the United States to extradite “manosphere” bloggers Andrew and Tristan Tate to the United Kingdom, calling the case an important step towards accountability for serious allegations of violence against women and girls.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Women do not stop giving birth in an emergency’ – one month after Venezuela quakes
item.description: One month after twin earthquakes rocked Venezuela, thousands of women and girls continue to face difficulty in accessing essential healthcare and protection services, a senior official with the UN reproductive and sexual health agency UNFPA said on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: In El Obeid, Sudanese women face drones by day, rape by night, to reach water
item.description: In El Obeid, women and girls now face an impossible choice over something as basic as a bucket of water: risk a drone strike by collecting it in daylight, or risk rape by waiting until dark.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Health response brings lifesaving care closer to thousands in Yemen
item.description: Thousands of people in some of Yemen's most conflict-affected communities are receiving lifesaving health care closer to home, thanks to funding from the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) through the Yemen Humanitarian Fund.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘I consider it a miracle’: Pregnant woman pulled from post-quake rubble in Venezuela
item.description: When a 12-story apartment building pancaked in La Guaira, Venezuela, following two powerful earthquakes late last month, panic ensued to save people injured or trapped under the rubble.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Independent expert urges UK leaders to uphold Supreme Court ruling on women’s rights
item.description: A UN independent human rights expert has urged political leaders in the United Kingdom to support implementation of a Supreme Court ruling on the legal definition of sex, warning that opposition to updated equality guidance risks weakening protections for women and girls.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Aid cuts leave at least one million women and girls without vital support
item.description: At least one million women and girls have lost access to critical humanitarian support since January 2025 as unprecedented aid cuts push women's organizations in crisis zones to the brink of collapse, the UN’s gender equality agency, UN Women, said on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Restoring dignity: Senegalese surgeon and Burundian foundation win reproductive health awards
item.description: A Senegalese surgeon who has dedicated his career to restoring the health and dignity of women living with obstetric fistula, and a Burundian foundation supporting vulnerable women and children, have been named the winners of the 2026 United Nations Population Award.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Students injured in Sudan drone strike, dangerous returns in south Lebanon, celebrating women diplomats
item.description: Ongoing fighting in the Sudanese city of El Obeid continues to endanger civilians and damage infrastructure, the United Nations said on Wednesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: AI is getting women wrong as gender bias persists, data reveals
item.description: As artificial intelligence reshapes how people work, communicate and access information, UN Women warned on Monday that the technology is reproducing old gender stereotypes, which amplify online abuse and leave women out of the decisions that will define the digital future.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Refugee turned peacemaker: The young woman leader transforming communities in the Central African Republic
item.description: In the heart of the Central African Republic (CAR), a nation long marked by conflict, Nina Mireille Yankinon stands as a symbol of resilience, leadership, and hope, dedicating her life to helping communities torn apart by war.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Grave concern’ after dozens of women arrested in Afghanistan for dress violations
item.description: Gender equality agency UN Women is “gravely concerned” by the arrest of at least 30 women in Herat city last weekend in Afghanistan for allegedly violating dress requirements imposed by Taliban authorities.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Women and girls cannot wait’: Lebanon’s crisis is putting lives at risk
item.description: Women and girls in Lebanon are paying an increasingly devastating price as violence and displacement continue despite a ceasefire, the UN reproductive health agency (UNFPA) warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Conflict-related sexual violence cases more than doubled in 2025, UN warns
item.description: Nearly 10,000 cases of conflict-related sexual violence were recorded worldwide last year – more than double the previous year's figure – as rape, sexual slavery and abduction were deployed as weapons of war across Africa, the Middle East, Europe and the Caribbean.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: War is becoming a death sentence for women and girls
item.description: Thirteen-year-old Mona still remembers the moment the second airstrike hit.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Afghan mothers and children face worsening hunger crisis, WFP warns
item.description: Afghanistan’s deepening malnutrition crisis is pushing mothers and children to the brink, the UN World Food Programme has warned, as mass returns from neighbouring countries and severe funding shortfalls overwhelm already strained humanitarian operations.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Chad’s refugee crisis overwhelms maternity care in east, UN agency warns
item.description: Many women in eastern Chad are being forced to give birth in overcrowded clinics with limited medicine, minimal equipment and severe shortages of anesthesia, as a worsening humanitarian crisis overwhelms the country’s fragile healthcare system, the UN reproductive health agency, UNFPA, warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Abuse of women journalists made ‘easier and more damaging’ by AI
item.description: Reports of online violence against women journalists have doubled since 2020, with serious impacts on their health and well-being, according to a study published ahead of World Press Freedom Day marked annually on 3 May.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Afghanistan risks losing 25,000 women teachers and health workers
item.description: Restrictions on girls’ education and women’s employment in Afghanistan could leave the country with a deficit of over 25,000 female teachers and health workers by 2030, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: A race for rights: How sport is helping protect girls in Uganda
item.description: On a red running track in eastern Uganda, coach Zuena Cheptoek is doing more than training runners. For many girls in the Sebei subregion, she is also a confidante, a mentor and first line of protection against female genital mutilation, child marriage and abuse.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Sudan: Three quarters of women feel unsafe as war rages on
item.description: Across war-torn Sudan, women and girls “are telling a consistent story of continued experience of danger, and risks for gender-based violence” whether when fleeing to safety or arriving at displacement camps, a senior official with the UN reproductive and sexual health agency UNFPA said on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: More than 38,000 women and girls killed in Gaza war, UN gender equality agency reports
item.description: The war in Gaza has inflicted a far higher toll on women and girls than in previous conflicts in the Palestinian enclave, with more than 38,000 killed by Israeli air bombardment and land military operations since Hamas-led terror attacks in Israel sparked the war in October 2023, UN Women said on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: The Epstein files: Rights experts demand accountability, call for probe into trafficking allegations
item.description: UN independent human rights experts called on Thursday for justice and accountability for young women and girls who were trafficked systematically as part of allegations contained in the so-called Epstein files.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: From misdiagnosis to medical bias: Why women are living longer but not better
item.description: For 25 years, the world has made significant progress in advancing women’s right to health, particularly in sexual and reproductive care. Women are living longer than ever before – but they are not living better.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Women leaders unite to advance gender equality, defend multilateralism amid growing global pushback
item.description: The Secretary-General’s commitment towards women leadership in the United Nations was recognized at a pivotal moment marked by global uncertainty, economic volatility and increasing pressure on hard-won rights.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: How Kyrgyzstan built a system to support domestic violence survivors
item.description: Domestic violence was not something people spoke about openly in Kyrgyzstan in the 1990s following the collapse of the Soviet Union, but after a long road of dedicated efforts, there are now laws addressing family abuse, crisis centres and hotlines while human rights defenders tackle such new challenges as sexual slavery.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
